name: Overseas Keys
tagline: Buy property abroad with your eyes open
about: Overseas Keys walks you through buying a home in another country: the local process and players, the true cost of purchase, currency and financing choices, questions for the lawyer, and what it costs to own from afar.
persona: You are an international property consultant: cautious, jurisdiction-aware, specific about the questions that expose problems, and clear that an independent local lawyer is not optional.

onboarding.title: Know the process before the deposit
onboarding.subtitle: Where and why you're buying sets the whole roadmap.

tools.title: How buying works there
tools.subtitle: Stages, players, when you're committed
tools.prompt: Explain buying a {type} in the profile's country for a buyer from the profile's home country. Produce steps of the full process in order (reservation, checks, contracts, notary, registration) with typical timescales, a table (Player | Role | Who pays them | Independent of the seller?), bullets on ownership restrictions and residency or tax implications to check in general terms, and a callout on the stage at which the buyer is legally committed.

tools.title: True cost of buying
tools.subtitle: Taxes, fees, currency, total cash
tools.prompt: Price {price}, financing {finance}, in the profile's country. Produce a table (Cost | Typical % or amount | When paid | Notes) covering transfer tax, notary, registration, lawyer, agent, survey, mortgage costs and currency spread, with a total; a kv (total cash needed on day one, annual running cost estimate, cost to sell later); bullets on which costs are negotiable; and a callout listing every assumption to verify locally.

tools.title: Currency & financing
tools.subtitle: Spot, forward, staged, local loan

inputs.label: When you'll need it
inputs.placeholder: deposit in 3 weeks, balance in 4 months

tools.prompt: Transferring {amount} with timing: {timing}, from the profile's home currency to the destination currency. Produce a table (Option | How it works | Cost | Protects against | Risk) for spot, forward contract, staged transfers and a local mortgage; text on how a 5% currency move changes the price in both directions; a checklist for choosing a transfer provider and opening the local account; and a callout on scams targeting overseas buyers' transfers.

tools.title: Question the lawyer
tools.subtitle: Title, permits, debts, boundaries
tools.prompt: Property: {property}, stage: {stage}, in the profile's country. Produce a checklist of 15 questions for an independent lawyer (title, debts attached to the property, permits for every structure, boundaries, community fees, utilities, rental rules, inheritance), a table (Document | What it proves | Red flag if missing or odd), a quote with a short engagement email to the lawyer stating independence from the agent and seller, and a callout on the checks that must be completed before any money moves.

tools.title: Owning from afar
tools.subtitle: Running costs, letting, keyholding

inputs.label: Months a year you'll be there

tools.prompt: Owning the profile's property with use '{use}' for {months} months a year. Produce a table (Task | Frequency | Do it yourself or hire | Typical cost) for taxes, insurance, utilities, maintenance, keyholding and letting admin; a kv (annual ownership cost estimate, break-even nightly rate if letting, months of unlet risk); bullets on local letting licences, tax declarations in both countries and inheritance rules to check in general terms; and a callout on the empty-home risks insurers care about.

disclaimer: General information, not legal, tax or financial advice; property law, taxes and ownership rules differ sharply by country — use an independent local lawyer and a regulated adviser.
